headline: Local Cabinet Minister resigns from WhatsApp family group after cousin fails to endorse his preferred breakfast menu
body:
State Minister for Small-Scale Infrastructure, Rajeshwar Rao, formally exited the 'Rao Family Union' WhatsApp group on Tuesday morning, citing a complete lack of consensus regarding his proposal to make Masala Dosa the official family breakfast preference.

The resignation followed a tense 48-hour thread where Rao insisted that all cousins, aunts, and distant uncles must publicly declare their preference for dosa over traditional poha. After his second cousin, Suresh, posted a photo of a bowl of Poha with a thumbs-up emoji, the Minister immediately triggered his exit protocol, citing an irreconcilable ideological split.

“It’s not about the breakfast; it’s about the lack of vision,” Rao said while drafting a 400-word follow-up statement to be emailed to all 84 group members. “If we cannot align our morning carb intake under a single, unified banner, how can I be expected to attend the Sunday joint-family lunch in good conscience? There is no room for multi-dish ambiguity in this household.”

Family elders have since attempted to mediate the crisis, offering a compromise of 'Idli-Poha unity' with a side of chutney. However, the Minister remains firm, stating he will only return to the digital conversation if a formal, notarized poll confirms his Dosa platform as the sole, undisputed breakfast candidate for the next five years.
caption: Ministerial standards are being applied to the most important things, like breakfast. Have you ever threatened to leave a group chat over a trivial disagreement? #FamilyDrama #BreakfastPolitics #DosaVsPoha (satire)

The named character 'Rajeshwar Rao' is a generic-sounding name not clearly identifying a real, specific high-profile cabinet minister, and the premise avoids any real-world political controversy, communal, or ethical harm.
